issues.title: Add Cancel button to Customer Contracts Create form
issues.description:
## User Story
As a user, I want a Cancel button on the Customer Contracts Create form so that I can navigate away without saving changes, with a confirmation prompt if I have entered any data.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Given I am on the Customer Contracts Create form
      When I click Cancel
      Then a Cancel button is visible on the form
- [ ] Given I am on the Customer Contracts Create form and have not entered any data
      When I click Cancel
      Then I am returned to the previous page without saving changes
- [ ] Given I am on the Customer Contracts Create form and have entered data into one or more fields
      When I click Cancel
      Then the existing confirmation modal is displayed warning me that my progress will be lost
- [ ] Given the confirmation modal is displayed
      When I confirm the cancellation
      Then I am returned to the previous page without saving changes
- [ ] Given the confirmation modal is displayed
      When I dismiss the modal
      Then I remain on the Customer Contracts Create form with my entered data intact

issues.title: Add Secondary Email and SMS tabs to Notification missing-contact list
issues.description:
## User Story
**As an** organization administrator,
**I want** individual tabs for Secondary Email and SMS on the Notification page's missing-contact list,
**So that** I can view and download targeted lists of users missing each specific contact type.

---

## Background / Context

**Current Behavior**
The Notification page shows a single consolidated list ("Employee Without Notification Information") of users who have not entered either a secondary email address or SMS number, with one CSV download for the combined list.

**Desired Behavior**
The consolidated list is restructured into three tabs:
- **All** — the current consolidated list (users missing secondary email OR SMS), with CSV download (preserves existing behavior)
- **Secondary Email** — users who have not entered a secondary email address, with CSV download
- **SMS** — users who have not entered an SMS number, with CSV download

Each tab displays the same columns as the current consolidated list (Employee, Secondary Email status, SMS status), filtered to the relevant contact type. The system remembers the user's last selected tab, so that tab will be the one that loads next time the user visits the page.

---

## Acceptance Criteria (Gherkin)

```gherkin
Feature: Tabbed missing-contact lists on the Notification page
  As an organization administrator
  I want individual tabs for Secondary Email and SMS on the Notification page's missing-contact list
  So that I can view and download targeted lists of users missing each specific contact type

  Background:
    Given I am signed in as an organization administrator
    And I am on the Notification page

  Scenario: Tabs are present on the Notification page
    When the missing-contact list section loads
    Then I see three tabs labeled "All", "Secondary Email", and "SMS"

  Scenario: "All" tab preserves existing consolidated behavior
    When I click the "All" tab
    Then I see the consolidated list of users missing a secondary email address OR an SMS number
    And the list displays the columns "Employee", "Secondary Email status", and "SMS status"
    And I can download the list as a CSV

  Scenario: "Secondary Email" tab shows users missing a secondary email
    When I click the "Secondary Email" tab
    Then I see only users who have not entered a secondary email address
    And the list displays the columns "Employee", "Secondary Email status", and "SMS status"
    And I can download the filtered list as a CSV

  Scenario: "SMS" tab shows users missing an SMS number
    When I click the "SMS" tab
    Then I see only users who have not entered an SMS number
    And the list displays the columns "Employee", "Secondary Email status", and "SMS status"
    And I can download the filtered list as a CSV

  Scenario Outline: CSV file names are distinguishable per tab
    Given I am viewing the "<tab>" tab
    When I download the list as a CSV
    Then the downloaded file name is "<file_name>"

    Examples:
      | tab              | file_name                   |
      | All              | missing-all.csv             |
      | Secondary Email  | missing-secondary-email.csv |
      | SMS              | missing-sms.csv             |

  Scenario: System remembers the last selected tab on return visit
    Given I have selected the "SMS" tab during my previous visit to the Notification page
    When I navigate away and later return to the Notification page
    Then the "SMS" tab is selected and loaded by default

  Scenario: Default tab on first visit
    Given I have never selected a tab on the Notification page before
    When I open the Notification page
    Then the "All" tab is selected by default
```

---

## Definition of Done
- All Gherkin scenarios above pass automated acceptance tests.
- UI matches existing styling/accessibility standards (keyboard navigation, ARIA roles for tabs).
- Last-selected-tab persistence works across sessions (e.g., stored per user).
- CSV exports validated for each tab (correct rows, correct file name).
- Updated documentation/help text reflects new tabbed view.
- Code reviewed, merged, and deployed to the test environment for stakeholder sign-off.

issues.title: Manual Update of User Responses for Notifications
issues.description:
## User Story

As a Notification Manager, I need the ability to manually update a user's response to a "response required" notification, so that I can accurately track acknowledgments when employee respond to me directly (out-of-band) rather than through the system.

## Acceptance Criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Manual update of user responses by Notification Manager

  Scenario: Notification Manager manually inputs a response for a pending user
    Given a "response required" notification has been distributed
    And a target user currently has a "pending" or "no response" status
    And the Notification Manager is viewing the response tracking or details page for that notification
    When the Notification Manager selects the option to manually update the response for the target user
    And the Notification Manager inputs the appropriate response value (e.g., Acknowledged, Yes/No)
    And the Notification Manager saves the manual entry
    Then the target user's status must immediately update to reflect the newly entered response
    And the system must log that the response was manually entered
    And the system must record the timestamp and identity of the Notification Manager who made the update

  Scenario: Notification Manager modifies a previously submitted user response
    Given a target user has an existing recorded response for a "response required" notification
    And the Notification Manager is viewing the response tracking or details page for that notification
    When the Notification Manager selects the option to edit the user's existing response
    And the Notification Manager inputs the corrected response value
    And the Notification Manager saves the manual entry
    Then the target user's status must immediately update to reflect the modified response
    And the system must retain a historical log of the previous response
    And the system must record the timestamp and identity of the Notification Manager who modified the response

  Scenario: Unauthorized users cannot manually update responses
    Given a user without the "Notification Manager" role is viewing the notification tracking page
    When the user attempts to view the individual user response statuses
    Then the option to manually update or edit another user's response must be disabled or hidden
```

## Behavioral Clarifications

### Once a response is set, it stays set

After a Notification Manager manually updates a user's response, **any subsequent text response from that user will not overwrite the manual entry**. The manager's deliberate update is treated as the source of truth. If a user replies via text after a manual update, that reply will not change the recorded value.

If the manager wants to revise the response again, they can — managers can edit a row as many times as needed, and each edit replaces the previous value.

### Where the edit option appears

- The pencil edit icon appears on every response row visible to a Notification Manager — pending rows, manually overridden rows, and rows where the user has already responded.
- Supervisors and other non-managers do not see the edit option on any row.

### Response options on the form

The dropdown of available responses on the edit form reflects the event's actual response configuration:
- For events with custom responses, the manager picks from the same custom options the user could have selected.
- For default events, the manager picks from "I'm okay" or "I need help."

This ensures the manually entered value is always one of the values the user could have legitimately replied with.

### Visual indicator on the tracking page

Rows on the Responses table that are currently a manual override show a small information icon next to the response value. Hovering reveals the manager who entered it and the date/time. Rows with an authentic response from the user have no indicator.

### CSV export changes

The Notification Event CSV download now has a new columns at the end of each response row:

- **`Manually Updated By`** 

The export captures both who made each change last.

### What's recorded in the audit trail

For every manual update the system records:

- **Who** — the name and persona ID of the Notification Manager who triggered that change.
- **When** — the date and time of that change (UTC).

### Authorization (Scenario 3 specifics)

The edit option is enforced in two places:
- The pencil icon is hidden in the UI for users without the Notification Manager role.
- A user who tries to bypass the UI (e.g., by pasting an edit URL directly) is rejected by the server and redirected to the notifications page with an error.

Supervisors and other non-managers see the responses tracking page in read-only form (no change from current behavior).

Plan CosmosDB multi-database architecture for migration
issues.description:
**Goal:** Define the target Cosmos DB for MongoDB database structure for the ORBIT migration to internal Azure CosmosDB.

**Driving constraints:**
- Cosmos shared-throughput cap of 25 collections per database (current ORBIT Mongo holds ~80).
- Scale target: 14,000 employee today → 100,000+ within ~12 months.
- Customer is the natural tenant boundary.

**Decisions captured:**
- Per-customer (one DB per customer) tenant model with a single consolidated DB per customer.
- Global DBs for identity/routing, reference lookups (split mil/geo), system telemetry.
- Notifications live in the per-customer tenant DB (organization owns its notification data).
- Existing `ORBIT-Queue` Mongo outbox migrates as-is (already its own DB, already under 25 collections).
- Downstream `orbitdata` SQL Server stays untouched.
- IT asset collections (`CustomerItAsset`, `CustomerItHandReceipt`) retired — not migrated.

**Open issue:** Tenant DB lands at ~31 collections after pulling notifications in — over the 25 cap.

issues.title: Persist filter tab and scope search by it on customer setting index pages
issues.description:
## User Story

As an Organization Manager or Admin,
I want the active/inactive/all filter on customer setting index pages to persist across page loads and to constrain the search results,
so that I can return to a list in the state I left it and only see records that match both my filter and my search at the same time.

## Background

Customer setting index pages with the **Active / All / Inactive** filter buttons are:

- `Areas/Customer/Views/Role/Index.cshtml`
- `Areas/Customer/Views/Layer/Index.cshtml`
- `Areas/Customer/Views/Task/Index.cshtml`
- `Areas/Customer/Views/Report/Index.cshtml`
- `Areas/Customer/Views/Matrix/Index.cshtml`
- `Areas/Customer/Views/WorkSite/Index.cshtml`
- `Areas/Customer/Views/Customer/Position.cshtml`
- `Areas/Customer/Views/Customer/Employee.cshtml`
- `Areas/Customer/Views/VendorAccount/Index.cshtml`
- `Areas/Customer/Views/Contract/Index.cshtml`

## Acceptance Criteria

### Scenario 1: Search respects the Active filter

```gherkin
Given I am on a customer setting index page that has the Active/All/Inactive filter
And the "Active" filter is selected
And the table contains both active and inactive records that match my search term
When I open the search field and type a search term
Then only active records that match the search term are shown
And inactive records that match the search term are hidden
And active records that do not match the search term are hidden
```

### Scenario 2: Search respects the Inactive filter

```gherkin
Given I am on a customer setting index page that has the Active/All/Inactive filter
And the "Inactive" filter is selected
And the table contains both active and inactive records that match my search term
When I open the search field and type a search term
Then only inactive records that match the search term are shown
And active records that match the search term are hidden
```

### Scenario 3: Search respects the All filter

```gherkin
Given I am on a customer setting index page that has the Active/All/Inactive filter
And the "All" filter is selected
When I open the search field and type a search term
Then both active and inactive records that match the search term are shown
And records that do not match the search term are hidden
```

### Scenario 5: Clearing the search restores the current filter view

```gherkin
Given I am on a customer setting index page that has the Active/All/Inactive filter
And the "Inactive" filter is selected
And I have typed a search term that hides some inactive rows
When I clear the search field
Then all inactive records are shown
And no active records are shown
```

### Scenario 6: Selected filter persists across page reloads

```gherkin
Given I am on a customer setting index page that has the Active/All/Inactive filter
And I select the "Inactive" filter
When I reload the page
Then the "Inactive" filter is selected
And only inactive records are shown
```

### Scenario 7: Selected filter persists when navigating away and returning

```gherkin
Given I am on the Customer Roles index page
And I select the "All" filter
When I navigate to a different page
And I navigate back to the Customer Roles index page
Then the "All" filter is selected
And both active and inactive records are shown
```

### Scenario 8: Persisted filter is per index page, not shared across pages

```gherkin
Given I have selected the "Inactive" filter on the Customer Roles index page
And I have selected the "All" filter on the Customer Layers index page
When I reload the Customer Roles index page
Then the "Inactive" filter is selected on the Customer Roles page
And the Customer Layers page still has the "All" filter selected when I navigate to it
```

### Scenario 9: First-time visit defaults to Active

```gherkin
Given I have never selected a filter on a customer setting index page
And I have no stored filter preference for that page
When I load the page
Then the "Active" filter is selected
And only active records are shown
```

## Implementation Notes

- The current search handler in `wwwroot/js/script.js` (around line 3462) calls `elementTableBodyRows.show()` before filtering by text — this is what causes search to ignore the Active/Inactive selection. Search must layer on top of the current filter rather than overwrite it.
- `filterContracts(filter)` (around `script.js:670`) and the page-load default at `script.js:809-811` both need to consult/update a `localStorage` key. A per-page key such as `customerFilter:<pathname>` keeps Scenario 8 straightforward.
- `closeSearch()` (around `script.js:3482`) resets all rows with `.show()` — it must re-apply the current filter rather than reveal everything.

issues.title: Build orbit-identity database and update entity classes
issues.description:
**Goal:** Build the `orbit-identity` Cosmos database — the routing front door for the new multi-database architecture. Holds the master `Employee` record plus person-attached audit/task collections. Includes both the Cosmos provisioning *and* the source-code change to route the corresponding entity classes to the new database.

**Collections (6) and shard keys:**
- `Employee` — shard on `PersonaId` today; switch to `EmployeeId` once the Employee ID key transition completes (coordinate with that work).
- `EmployeeAudit` — shard on `EmployeeId` (colocates a person's audit history).
- `EmployeeTask` — shard on `EmployeeId` (colocates a person's tasks).
- `SystemAdministrator` — shard on `_id`.
- `SystemSignIn` — shard on `_id`.
- `WebSession` — shard on `_id`.

**Scope of this issue:**

*Database / infrastructure work:*
- Provision the `orbit-identity` database in TESTENV Cosmos for MongoDB (internal).
- Create each collection above with the correct shard key.
- Validate connectivity from a worker pod (X.509 auth, RU floor sizing).

*Source-code work:*
- Apply the `[Database(DatabaseScope.GlobalNamed, "orbit-identity")]` attribute to each of the six entity classes:
  - `ORBIT.Model.Employee` (already done in the Entity<T> refactor verification)
  - `ORBIT.Model.EmployeeAudit`
  - `ORBIT.Model.EmployeeTask`
  - `ORBIT.Model.SystemAdministrator`
  - `ORBIT.Model.SystemSignIn`
  - `ORBIT.Model.WebSession`
- After applying, do a clean **rebuild** (Build → Rebuild Solution) — hot reload silently skips changes to static field initializers, which is what the `[Database]` attribute resolver depends on.
- Verify reads *and* writes both land on `orbit-identity` for each entity (the Employee verification turned up that writes were going through a separate code path until `Entity<T>.Save(BsonDocument)` was also routed through `ResolveDatabaseName()` — the same care applies for these other classes if they have any custom `Save()` overrides).

*Migration-script work:*
- Add `$out` aggregations to `MongoDB/Migrate.js` to copy each of the six collections from `ORBIT.{collection}` into `orbit-identity.{collection}`.

**Out of scope for this issue (tracked separately):**
- Migration scripts that span ALL the global/tenant databases — this issue covers only the `orbit-identity` slice.
- Production cutover (per the Migration Phases plan in the design doc).

**Reference:** `CosmosDB-Migration-Design.md` — see the `orbit-identity` section under "Target Database Layout" and the partition-key guidance under "Migration script design".

issues.title: Build orbit-system database and update entity classes
issues.description:
**Goal:** Build the `orbit-system` Cosmos database — append-only telemetry and log streams. High insert volume (`ApplicationLog` is the largest), low read volume. Includes both the Cosmos provisioning *and* the source-code change to route the corresponding entity classes to the new database.

**Collections (4) — all shard on `_id`:**
- `ApplicationLog` — structured application log; **highest insert volume in the post-retirement system**.
- `ResponseTime` — per-request response time trace (replaces the discontinued `SystemResponse`).
- `SystemLog` — general system log.
- `ReminderLog` — reminder send log.

**Partition key rationale:** `_id` (`ObjectId`) already has a timestamp prefix, so it distributes inserts evenly across logical partitions without creating a hot "today" partition that a date-truncated key would. No specialized key needed for these access patterns.

**Scope of this issue:**

*Database / infrastructure work:*
- Provision the `orbit-system` database in TESTENV Cosmos for MongoDB (internal).
- Create each collection above with `_id` as the shard key.
- **Configure TTL indexes on each collection** for 30-day rolling retention. Without TTL, these collections grow unbounded — `ApplicationLog` would dominate storage cost within months. The TTL field is `DateCreated` on every collection.
- Validate connectivity from a worker pod (X.509 auth, RU floor sizing).

*Source-code work:*
- Apply the `[Database(DatabaseScope.GlobalNamed, "orbit-system")]` attribute to the four entity classes in `ORBIT.Model.Log`:
  - `ORBIT.Model.Log.Application` (the `ApplicationLog` class)
  - `ORBIT.Model.Log.ResponseTime`
  - `ORBIT.Model.Log.SystemLog`
  - `ORBIT.Model.Log.Reminder` (the `ReminderLog` class)
- After applying, do a clean **rebuild** (Build → Rebuild Solution) — hot reload silently skips changes to static field initializers, which is what the `[Database]` attribute resolver depends on.
- Verify reads *and* writes both land on `orbit-system` for at least one representative class — telemetry write paths are scattered across the codebase (every controller does some logging), so a smoke test with a single page-load and an mongosh check is sufficient.

*Migration-script work:*
- Add `$out` aggregations to `MongoDB/Migrate.js` to copy each of the four collections from `ORBIT.{collection}` into `orbit-system.{collection}`. Same pattern as `orbit-lookup` — no checkpointing needed at this scale, and the data is append-only telemetry so any in-flight write loss during cutover is non-critical.

**Out of scope for this issue (tracked separately):**

**Note on isolation:** keeping telemetry in its own database matters because the insert firehose (`ApplicationLog` especially) should not compete for RU/s with user-blocking identity reads on `orbit-identity`. Provision RU/s independently per database.

**Reference:** `CosmosDB-Migration-Design.md` — see the `orbit-system` section under "Target Database Layout".

issues.title: Build orbit-tenant per-customer databases and update entity classes
issues.description:
**Goal:** Build the per-customer `orbit-tenant-{customerId}` Cosmos databases — one database per customer holding the full operational footprint for that organization. This is the largest piece of the migration: N databases (one per customer, ~29 in TESTENV), 23 collections each, plus the runtime tenant-resolution machinery that routes every request to the right database.

**Collections (23) and shard keys:**

*Sharded on `_id` (18 collections):*
- `Customer`
- `CustomerContract`
- `CustomerVendorAccount`
- `CustomerWorkSite`
- `CustomerLayer`
- `CustomerMatrix`
- `CustomerReport`
- `CustomerRole`
- `CustomerSoftwareLicense`
- `CustomerTask`
- `CustomerTaskAudit`
- `NotificationEvent`
- `NotificationGroup`
- `NotificationScenario`
- `OooItem`
- `OooLog`
- `OooLogParent`
- `CheckInHot`

*Sharded on `EmployeeId` (3 collections — colocates a person's records, used by the employee-detail page query patterns):*
- `CheckIn` *(largest collection in the system)*
- `NotificationLog`
- `NotificationResponse`

*Sharded on `CustomerLayerId` (2 collections — colocates positions within an org layer):*
- `Tda`
- `TdaPosition`

**Scope of this issue:**

*Database / infrastructure work:*
- Provision one `orbit-tenant-{customerId}` database in TESTENV Cosmos for MongoDB (internal) per existing customer (~29 today).
- Create each of the 23 collections per database with the correct shard key (see above).
- Validate connectivity from a worker pod (X.509 auth, RU floor sizing). Plan for per-tenant RU/s budgets — large customers may need different floors than small ones.

*Source-code work:*
- Apply the `[Database(DatabaseScope.Tenant)]` attribute to all 23 entity classes. Most live in `ORBIT.Model.Customer/`, `ORBIT.Model.CheckIn/`, and `ORBIT.Model.Notification/`. `Tda`, `TdaPosition`, `OooItem`, `OooLog`, and `OooLogParent` are in `ORBIT.Model` root. **`ORBIT.Model.Notification/*` code is off-limits to edit per CLAUDE.md** — adding the attribute on the class line is permitted (it's not a logic change), but the rest of those files stays untouched.
- Implement `CosmosTenantProvisioner` (sketched in `CosmosDB-Migration-Design.md` under the `orbit-tenant-{customerId}` section). Hook it into `Customer.Save()` so a brand-new customer automatically gets a provisioned tenant DB with all 23 collections sharded correctly.
- Wire the web layer's auth middleware to call `TenantContext.Use(employee.CustomerId)` once per request after authentication resolves the user's customer. Until this is in place, any `[Database(Tenant)]` entity access from the web layer will throw `InvalidOperationException("No tenant in scope.")`.
- Update worker services (`Background`, `Notification`, `Ooo`, `SqlReporting`) to wrap per-customer iteration in `using (TenantContext.Use(customer.Id)) { ... }` blocks. **`ORBIT.WorkerService.Notification` and `ORBIT.WorkerService.SqlReporting` are off-limits per CLAUDE.md** — coordinate with whoever owns those workers before touching them.
- After applying, do a clean **rebuild** (Build → Rebuild Solution) — hot reload silently skips changes to static field initializers.
- Verify reads *and* writes both land on the correct `orbit-tenant-{customerId}` database for at least one customer. The roll-call submission flow is a good smoke test — it touches `Customer`, `CustomerLayer`, `CustomerRole`, `CheckIn`, and `CheckInHot` in a single request.

*Migration-script work:*
- The per-tenant migration is more complex than the global DBs: you need to iterate `ORBIT.Customer`, and for each customer copy the 23 tenant collections from `ORBIT.{collection}` filtered by `Customer._id` into `orbit-tenant-{customerId}.{collection}`. Use `$match` before `$out` in the aggregation:
  ```javascript
  const customers = sourceDb.Customer.find({}, { _id: 1 }).toArray();
  for (const { _id: customerId } of customers) {
    const tenantDb = db.getSiblingDB(`orbit-tenant-${customerId}`);
    sourceDb.CheckIn.aggregate([
      { $match: { "Customer._id": customerId } },
      { $out: { db: tenantDb.getName(), coll: "CheckIn" } }
    ]);
    // ... repeat for the other 22 tenant collections
  }
  ```
- Wrap each call in the `copyIfMissing` pattern from `MongoDB/Migrate.js` so the script is idempotent across dev iterations.

**Out of scope for this issue (tracked separately):**
- Production cutover (per the Migration Phases plan in the design doc).
- Replacing the SQL Queue / `orbitdata` plumbing (out of scope for the entire migration).

**Reference:** `CosmosDB-Migration-Design.md` — see the `orbit-tenant-{customerId}` section under "Target Database Layout", the `CosmosTenantProvisioner` code sketch, and the Code Changes Required section for the `[Database(Tenant)]` + `TenantContext` runtime pattern.

Build Python script to migrate TEST MongoDB to TEST CosmosDB
issues.description:
**Goal:** Build a Python migration script that copies ORBIT data from the **TEST MongoDB** instance to the **TEST CosmosDB for MongoDB** instance, mirroring the logical structure of `MongoDB/Migrate.js` but operating across two different database instances. The script runs from a internal VDI that has network access to both endpoints.

**Why Python (not mongosh / Node.js):**
- mongosh `$out` only writes within a single MongoDB instance — cannot copy across servers.
- Python (`pymongo`) handles two independent connection strings cleanly, supports idempotent/resumable patterns, and matches the team's existing operational tooling (`md_to_pdf.py`, `create_issue.py`, etc.).
- Ships with Python 3 already on the internal VDI; only `pip install pymongo` is needed.

**Source / target shape:**
- **Source:** TEST MongoDB instance (single `ORBIT` database with all original collections, plus `ORBIT-Queue`).
- **Target:** TEST CosmosDB for MongoDB instance — empty, will receive the new multi-database structure: `orbit-identity`, `orbit-lookup`, `orbit-geo`, `orbit-system`, `ORBIT-Queue`, plus `orbit-tenant-{customerId}` per active customer.

**Scope of this issue:**

*Script:*
- New file `MongoDB/migrate.py` parallel to `Migrate.js`.
- Reads two env vars: `ORBIT_TEST_MONGODB_URI` (source) and `ORBIT_TEST_COSMOSDB_URI` (target).
- Mirrors the collection lists in `Migrate.js` exactly — global DBs (identity / geo / lookup / system / `ORBIT-Queue`) plus per-customer tenant DBs.
- Honors the same exclusions: skips `OooItem`, `CustomerItAsset`, `CustomerItHandReceipt`, `Travel`, `CustomerMetric`, `SystemPerformance`, `SystemPerformanceViewer`, `CheckInLocation`, `DaylightSaving`, `ItAssetType`, `SystemResponse`.
- **Idempotent:** re-runnable. Uses a checkpoint collection on the target side (`orbit-migration-control._checkpoint`) recording per-`(target_db, collection)` progress.
- **Resumable:** `_id` cursor with batched `bulk_write` upserts so a crash mid-collection resumes from the last completed batch (matters for `CheckIn` which has 3M+ documents).
- Per-customer slicing: iterates `ORBIT.Customer` and copies tenant collections filtered by `Customer._id`.
- `Customer` itself goes to `orbit-identity` (global), per the latest design.

*Operational:*
- Document the environment-variable contract and prerequisites in a `MongoDB/README.md` section (or inline at the top of `migrate.py`).
- Document how to run it from the internal VDI: `pip install pymongo`, set the two env vars, `python migrate.py`.

**Out of scope for this issue:**
- Production migration (cutover plan covered separately by the design doc's Migration Phases section).
- Data validation / reconciliation tooling beyond the per-collection counts emitted by the script (a richer validation pass can be its own future issue).
- Performance tuning for production-scale CheckIn (will surface during rehearsal, not now).

**Verification:**
- Run from internal VDI against TEST MongoDB → TEST CosmosDB.
- Log output should print `[copy]` / `[skip]` per collection (matching the JS script's vocabulary).
- Spot-check counts in target Cosmos vs. source MongoDB after a clean run.
- Re-run: every line should print `[skip]` (idempotency check).

**Reference:** `CosmosDB-Migration-Design.md` — see "Migration script design" subsection for the idempotent/resumable pattern. `MongoDB/Migrate.js` is the structural blueprint.

issues.title: Renaming a Customer Layer Name orphans existing CustomerLayer references; edit/save then fails
issues.description:
**Reported in:** INC0034282

**Symptom (from internal GitLab description):**
If a Layer Name (e.g. PM, PD, PL) is changed in an organization (e.g. PM -> Prod Man), any layers that exist in that organization can no longer be edited. The Layer Edit form shows the top-level Layer Name in a disabled selector, and Save returns 'Information was not saved' regardless of whether changes were made. Renaming back to the original does not resolve the issue. Newly created layers work correctly.

**Root cause:**
`CustomerLayerName.Save(Customer)` at `Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Model/Customer/LayerName.cs` unsets the entire `LayerNameList` and rebuilds it with brand-new `ObjectId` values for **every** entry on every save — even ones that were not renamed. Existing `CustomerLayer` documents still embed the old `LayerName._id` values, which are now orphaned.

When a CustomerLayer is then edited:
1. The Form (`Areas/Customer/Views/Layer/Form.cshtml`) builds the Layer `<select>` from the customer's new `LayerNameList` — the previously selected ID is no longer in the list, so no option is selected and the disabled dropdown shows the first option (the top-level name).
2. The hidden `LayerName.Id` posted back is the orphaned ID.
3. `CustomerLayer.ToBsonDocument()` calls `CustomerLayerName.FetchById(this.LayerName.Id)`, which returns null, then dereferences `this.LayerName.LayerLevel` → `NullReferenceException`.
4. `LayerController.Save()` catches and redirects to `?error=1` (the 'Information was not saved' banner).

**Fix (Option 1 – preserve IDs):**
Modify `CustomerLayerName.Save()` to match each incoming form entry to an existing entry by `LayerLevel` and reuse its `_id`. Only generate a new `ObjectId` for layer levels that did not exist before. Drop the redundant `Unset` of `LayerNameList` (the trailing `Set` replaces it).

**Tests to add:**
- Failing test that proves `CustomerLayerName.Save()` currently regenerates IDs for unchanged entries.
- (After fix) regression test that asserts IDs are preserved across a rename.

**Files in scope:**
- `Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Model/Customer/LayerName.cs` (fix)
- `Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Test.Unit/Customer/LayerNames.cs` (tests)

issues.title: Fix supervisor reminder email — NullReferenceException on missing TimeZone.Name
issues.description:
**Component:** `ORBIT.WorkerService.Background` → `ORBIT.Model.Reminder.Email.SupervisorDidNotReportEmployee`

**Symptom:** Customer reported their supervisor was not receiving the morning 'did not report' supervisor email.

**Root cause:** The employee filter in `SupervisorDidNotReportEmployee()` called `t.WorkSite.TimeZone.Name.StartsWith( timeZoneId )` without first checking that `Name` was non-null. If any one employee record system-wide had a `WorkSite.TimeZone` with a null `Name`, the `.ToList()` threw a `NullReferenceException`. Because the 9:30 trigger in `Worker.ExecuteAsync` calls the method via `Task.Run(...)` with no `await` and no try/catch, the exception became an unobserved task exception — silently swallowed — and no supervisor received the email that morning.

The sibling method `RemindToReport()` already had the `!String.IsNullOrEmpty(t.WorkSite.TimeZone.Name)` guard; `SupervisorDidNotReportEmployee()` did not.

**Fix:** Added the matching `!String.IsNullOrEmpty(t.WorkSite.TimeZone.Name)` guard in the LINQ filter at `Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Model/Reminder/Email.cs`.

issues.title: Fix mobile check-in: capture free-text note after menu option
issues.description:
**File:** `Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Model/Telephony/CheckIn.cs`

**Bug:** When a user texts a mobile check-in with extra text after the menu option (e.g. `4 Going to meeting`), only the menu option (`4`) is captured. The free-text remainder (`Going to meeting`) is parsed out as `messageRemainder` and passed into `Process(...)` as the `message` argument, but the switch statement only consumes it for cases 3 and 8 (Travel / Off-Site, for geographic parsing). For all other menu options the remainder is silently discarded, and `checkIn.Note` only contains the hard-coded `"Reported by Mobile Check-In with: '4'"`.

**Fix:** After setting the auto-generated note in `Process(...)`, append the trimmed `message` (when non-empty) to `checkIn.Note` as an additional `Note:` line. Applies to all menu options.

**Resulting note for `4 Going to meeting`:**
```
Reported by Mobile Check-In with: '4'

Note: Going to meeting
```
